nodes.label: AI for Science: Reframing AI's Role in Discovery
nodes.author: Kyle Cranmer, Neil D. Lawrence, Jessica Montgomery, Denis Thérien
nodes.rationale: Position paper examining AI's role in science; distinguishes paradigm shifts from normal science; addresses technical and institutional challenges

nodes.label: Task Capabilities Framework
nodes.rationale: First dimension of AI-for-science framework; distinguishes what different AI tools can deliver in practice

nodes.label: Scientific Workflow Needs
nodes.rationale: Second dimension of framework; identifies where AI adds value across hypothesis generation, experimental design, data analysis

nodes.label: Scientific Context and Constraints
nodes.rationale: Third dimension of framework; recognizes practical constraints (data, compute, validation requirements, domain tolerance for uncertainty)

nodes.label: The Science Gap: Pattern Matching vs Causal Reasoning
nodes.rationale: Central challenge: AI excels at pattern identification but struggles to identify causal mechanisms; gap between statistical and scientific reasoning

nodes.label: Causality in AI Systems
nodes.rationale: Technical priority: embedding causal structure in models to distinguish spurious correlations from causal relationships

nodes.label: Abstraction and Multi-Scale Discovery
nodes.rationale: Technical priority: discovering intermediate scales bridging different levels of explanation; key to scientific breakthroughs

nodes.label: Hybrid Mechanistic-Data-Driven Simulation
nodes.rationale: Technical priority: combining mechanistic models with data-driven flexibility to avoid oversimplification or physical implausibility

nodes.label: AI as Repository vs Interface
nodes.rationale: Epistemological question: whether AI encodes knowledge as parameters or provides conduit to external sources; implications for knowledge evolution

nodes.label: Human Understanding in Scientific Discovery
nodes.rationale: Philosophical question: whether science requires human comprehension or whether autonomous AI discovery is scientifically valid

nodes.label: Governance Gap in AI for Science
nodes.rationale: Institutional challenge: policy-practice gap in addressing bias, consent, privacy, transparency, reproducibility, and attribution

nodes.label: Research Culture Gap
nodes.rationale: Institutional challenge: limited career pathways for interdisciplinary AI-science researchers; funding mechanisms poorly adapted to team science

nodes.label: Infrastructure Gap and Compute Concentration
nodes.rationale: Institutional challenge: AI infrastructure concentrated in private companies; threatens open science and scientific independence

nodes.label: Discourse Gap and Narrative Dominance
nodes.rationale: Institutional challenge: corporate AI narratives dominate public discourse; obscure foundational public research and interdisciplinary teamwork

nodes.label: Paradigm Shift Question
nodes.rationale: Central question: whether AI represents normal science within computational paradigm or signals fundamental shift in what counts as scientific knowledge

nodes.label: Productivity Paradox in Science
nodes.rationale: Concern: scientific output growing but productivity declining; AI risks intensifying disconnect between output and progress

hyperedges.label: AI for Science: Technical and Institutional Challenges
